lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.title: Performance task planning: systems from contexts

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: This example shows how to justify a modelling choice.

items.prompt: Plan A charges a $10 flat fee plus $3 per month. Plan B charges a $4 flat fee plus $5 per month. After how many months do the two plans cost the same, and what is that cost?

steps: Set the two cost expressions equal: 10 + 3x = 4 + 5x.
Subtract 3x and 4 from both sides: 6 = 2x, so x = 3.
Substitute x = 3 into either plan to get a cost of 19, so the plans cost the same after 3 months at $19.

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Decide what the quantities are before you compute anything.

items.prompt: Plan A charges a $31 flat fee plus $9 per month. Plan B charges a $37 flat fee plus $6 per month. The solution to the system is (2, 49). What does this solution represent?
choices: Plan A costs $49 more than Plan B after 2 months.

items.prompt: System: y = -x + 1 and y = 3x - 3. Does the point (2, -1) satisfy both equations, fail one, or fail both?
Plan A charges a $71 flat fee plus $11 per month. Plan B charges a $77 flat fee plus $10 per month. The solution to the system is (6, 137). What does the y-coordinate of the solution represent?
choices: The number of months after which the two plans cost the same.
The shared cost, in dollars, when the two plans are equal.
The difference in cost between the two plans.
The rate Plan B charges per month.

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Plan in writing: what you will model, why that model, and how you will check it.

items.prompt: System: y = -4x + 34 and y = -2x + 20. Which point (x, y) satisfies both equations?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: Solve the system: y = x + 21 and y = -9x - 129. What is the intersection point (x, y)?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: Relationship A: x: 6, 7, 8, 9 y: -13, -8, -3, 2. Relationship B: x: 6, 7, 8, 9 y: 15, 6, -3, -12. At which x-value do the two relationships have the same y-value?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
